problems.source_says: The paper explicitly states that participants were randomly assigned to treatments, but does not establish individual versus session treatment allocation. It also refers to sessions conducted under the tournament condition. Appendix A specifies random assignment to four-person tournament groups, which does not identify the unit of treatment randomization. The form acknowledges this ambiguity in its narrative yet codes the unit definitively as individual; the unit should remain unconfirmed (null).
problems.quote: tournament entrants are matched with participants from sessions conducted under the tournament condition
problems.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 5), Section 2.1, Stage 2 (Competition Choice) and Experimental Procedures; PDF pp. 30-32 (appendix pp. 1-3), Appendix A.1. The complete document and appendices provide no further specification of the treatment-randomization unit.

confirmed.statement: S1: The abstract explicitly states random assignment to ChatGPT access or no access; the methods separately state that participants were randomly assigned to treatments.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Abstract, opening sentence; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 5), Section 2.1, Experimental Procedures.

confirmed.statement: S1: AI access was available while participants wrote their own creative compositions, satisfying the assistance requirement of criterion 1.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-8 (printed pp. 3-5), Section 2.1; PDF p. 31 (appendix p. 2), Appendix A.1, Instructions for Phase 1.

confirmed.statement: S1: The document identifies the writing assistant as the generative large language model ChatGPT-4.2, delivered through an API embedded in oTree.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Abstract; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4), Section 2.1; PDF p. 27 (printed p. 24), declaration of AI use.

confirmed.statement: S1: Participants could submit unrestricted requests through the writing screen; access ended when they completed the composition and proceeded to the next phase.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 31 (appendix p. 2), Appendix A.1, Instructions for Phase 1; unrestricted interaction also stated on PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4), Section 2.1.

confirmed.statement: S1: The six arms cross AI versus no AI with tournament, piece-rate and lottery incentives, matching T, PR, L, T&AI, PR&AI and L&AI in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-7 (printed pp. 3-4), Section 2.1; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 column headings.

confirmed.statement: S1: Piece-rate pays 0.6 times the average score; tournament pays the highest-scoring member of a gender-balanced group of four 2.4 euros per point and others zero; lottery randomly pays one of four 15 euros independently of performance.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4), Section 2.1, incentive-scheme bullets.

confirmed.statement: S1: The design is explicitly between subjects; randomized order of AI and no-AI conditions is therefore not applicable.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-7 (printed pp. 3-4), Section 2.1, design description and rationale for avoiding a within-subjects design.

confirmed.statement: S1: Random assignment of texts to external evaluators is a separate rating procedure; the laboratory manipulation concerns writers receiving AI access.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 5), Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 6), Section 2.2, rater assignment and blinding.

confirmed.statement: S1: Access was assigned, while submitting queries was optional; the form correctly distinguishes self-selected AI use from the randomized access comparison.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Abstract; PDF p. 31 (appendix p. 2), Appendix A.1; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1 notes defining AI (use).

confirmed.statement: S1: Table 1 confirms analyzed arm counts of 52, 47, 49, 88, 62 and 62 in the form's arm order, and AI-use proportions of 0.818, 0.677 and 0.790 in the three AI arms.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1, Obs. and AI (use) rows.

summary: The definite individual assignment unit is unsupported because individual versus session allocation remains unresolved. Criterion 1 still holds: the paper explicitly reports random assignment to ChatGPT access versus no AI for participants' own creative writing.
